questions.question: Who wrote Alice's Adventures in Wonderland?
questions.expected_answer: Lewis Carroll.

questions.question: How many chapters are listed, and what is the final chapter called?
questions.expected_answer: There are twelve chapters; the final chapter is Alice's Evidence.

questions.question: What color were the White Rabbit's eyes?
questions.expected_answer: Pink.

questions.question: What was disappointing about the orange marmalade jar?
questions.expected_answer: It was empty.
evidence_phrases: to her great disappointment it was empty

questions.question: What was the name of Alice's cat?
questions.expected_answer: Dinah.

questions.question: Approximately how tall was the little door Alice found?
questions.expected_answer: About fifteen inches high.
evidence_phrases: little door about fifteen inches high

questions.question: Which foods did Alice say the DRINK ME bottle tasted like?
questions.expected_answer: Cherry tart, custard, pineapple, roast turkey, toffee, and hot buttered toast.
evidence_phrases: mixed flavour of cherrytart, custard, pine-apple, roast turkey, toffee, and hot buttered toast

questions.question: What words were marked in currants on the cake?
questions.expected_answer: EAT ME.
evidence_phrases: words ‘EAT ME’ were beautifully marked in currants

questions.question: How tall did Alice become, and how deep was the pool of tears?
questions.expected_answer: Alice became more than nine feet tall, and the pool was about four inches deep.

questions.question: What caused Alice to start shrinking while she was talking to the Mouse?
questions.expected_answer: The Rabbit's fan she was holding.
evidence_phrases: cause of this was the fan she was holding

questions.question: Why did Alice address the Mouse in French?
questions.expected_answer: She remembered that a French mouse had come over with William the Conqueror.
evidence_phrases: French mouse, come over with William the Conqueror

questions.question: What activity did the Dodo recommend to get everyone dry?
questions.expected_answer: A Caucus-race.
evidence_phrases: best thing to get us dry would be a Caucus-race

questions.question: What prizes did Alice and the other racers receive after the Caucus-race?
questions.expected_answer: The others received comfits from Alice, and Alice received her own thimble from the Dodo.

questions.question: What did the White Rabbit order 'Mary Ann' to fetch?
questions.expected_answer: A pair of gloves and a fan.
evidence_phrases: Run home this moment, and fetch me a pair of gloves and a fan

questions.question: What name was engraved on the brass plate at the Rabbit's house?
questions.expected_answer: W. RABBIT.

questions.question: What did the pebbles thrown through the window become, and what happened when Alice ate one?
questions.expected_answer: They became little cakes, and eating one made Alice shrink.
evidence_phrases: pebbles were all turning into little cakes

questions.question: What different effects did the two sides of the mushroom have?
questions.expected_answer: One side made Alice grow taller and the other made her grow shorter.
evidence_phrases: One side will make you grow taller, and the other side will make you grow shorter

questions.question: Why did the Pigeon call Alice a serpent?
questions.expected_answer: The Pigeon was guarding eggs and concluded that Alice was a serpent because Alice admitted that little girls eat eggs too.
evidence_phrases: As if it wasn’t trouble enough hatching the eggs
little girls eat eggs quite as much as serpents do

questions.question: What invitation did the Fish-Footman deliver to the Duchess?
questions.expected_answer: An invitation from the Queen to play croquet.
evidence_phrases: An invitation from the Queen to play croquet

questions.question: Which two residents did the Cheshire Cat direct Alice toward, and what did it say about them?
questions.expected_answer: The Hatter and the March Hare; the Cat said they were both mad.

questions.question: What did the Duchess's baby turn into?
questions.expected_answer: A pig.

questions.question: Who was at the tea table, and what beverage did the March Hare falsely offer Alice?
questions.expected_answer: The March Hare, Hatter, and Dormouse were there; the March Hare offered wine even though there was none.

questions.question: Why was it always tea-time at the Hatter's table?
questions.expected_answer: Time had stopped at six o'clock, so it was always tea-time.

questions.question: What served as the balls, mallets, and arches in the Queen's croquet game?
questions.expected_answer: Hedgehogs were the balls, flamingoes were the mallets, and soldiers bent over to form the arches.

questions.question: According to the Duchess, under what condition does everything have a moral?
questions.expected_answer: If only you can find it.
evidence_phrases: Everything’s got a moral, if only you can find it

questions.question: Which oddly named subjects did the Mock Turtle say were taught at school?
questions.expected_answer: Reeling and Writhing, plus Ambition, Distraction, Uglification, and Derision.

questions.question: What final actions complete the first figure of the Lobster Quadrille?
questions.expected_answer: The dancers change lobsters and retire in the same order, then return to land to finish the first figure.
evidence_phrases: change lobsters, and retire in same order
Back to land again, and that’s all the first figure

questions.question: What was the Knave of Hearts accused of, and who was called as the first witness?
questions.expected_answer: He was accused of stealing the Queen's tarts, and the Hatter was the first witness.
evidence_phrases: The Knave of Hearts, he stole those tarts
The first witness was the Hatter

questions.question: Who was the next witness after the Hatter, and what did she say the tarts were mostly made of?
questions.expected_answer: The Duchess's cook; she said the tarts were mostly made of pepper.
evidence_phrases: next witness was the Duchess’s cook

questions.question: Under Rule Forty-two, which people had to leave the court?
questions.expected_answer: All persons more than a mile high.
